section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that natural conduct corresponds to the lower Daat, where creations have presence, while miraculous conduct corresponds to the upper Daat, and these two Daat correspond to Chochmah and Binah respectively.
section.t: And the explanation of the matter
(the connection of miracles to the inner union of Chochmah and Binah)
in more detail,
will be understood by prefacing what was explained above
(in the discourse beginning "Patah Eliyahu"9)
that the conduct of nature
[where the Holy One, blessed be He, conducts every creature according to its nature,
for this indicates that in this conduct the creations have place]
is in the aspect of the lower Daat, where below there is yesh (existence),
(and above there is not),
and miraculous conduct
[where the Holy One, blessed be He, conducts the world according to His will and not according to the nature and property of the creations,
for this indicates that in this conduct the creations do not have place]
is in the aspect of the upper Daat, where
(above there is yesh and)
below there is not.
And these two Daat in the matter of the Sefiros are Chochmah and Binah10.
For in Chochmah it is felt that Ein Sof is the true reality and everything before Him is considered as nothing11
— this is the upper Daat, where above there is yesh and below there is not,
and in Binah, which is comprehension,
for comprehension is a yesh existence,
it is the lower Daat.
For although even in Binah it is comprehended that everything before Him is considered as nothing,
this is not felt in it12.
For since comprehension
(even the comprehension that everything before Him is considered as nothing)
is an existence,
the existence
(of the comprehension)
is the opposite of the feeling of being considered as nothing13.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the lower Daat in Binah, where above there is not and below there is yesh, also applies to the flow from Chochmah to Binah, as the yesh of Binah comes from the concealment of the ayin of Chochmah.
section.t: And14 this that in Binah is the lower Daat, where above there is not and below there is yesh, is also regarding the flow from Chochmah to Binah.
For Chochmah and Binah are ayin (nothingness) and yesh (existence),
and the coming into being of Binah from Chochmah is analogous to the coming into being of yesh from ayin15.
For just as in the coming into being of yesh from ayin, the ayin is in concealment from the yesh,
therefore it is called by the name ayin because it is not grasped in the yesh
[And that the ayin is not grasped in the yesh is not only from the side of the yesh
(for it is incommensurate with the ayin and therefore cannot grasp the ayin),
but also from the side of the ayin,
for it
(the ayin)
conceals itself from the yesh.
And as is known16
that the coming into being of yesh from ayin is by means of the Divine power
(the ayin)
that brings the creature into existence
(the yesh)
concealing itself from the creature],
so too is it in the coming into being of Binah from Chochmah,
for that Binah is yesh is because the ayin of Chochmah conceals itself from Binah.
And although the comprehension of Binah is in the point of Chochmah,
for Binah comprehends the point of intellect,
nevertheless, the essence of Chochmah is the vision of Chochmah that is above intellect,
and this matter is not drawn into Binah at all.
And also the intellect of Chochmah
(that is drawn into Binah)
is
(primarily)
the laying down of the soul,
and the intellect within it is only the externality17.
And what is grasped in Binah is only the intellect within the point of intellect
(the externality),
but the laying down within the point of intellect
(its inwardness and essentiality)
is in the aspect of ayin relative to Binah,
for it is not grasped in it.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the upper Daat is specifically in Chochmah due to its inwardness and essentiality above intellect, while in Binah only the intellect of Chochmah is drawn, making it the lower Daat.
section.t: And based on this, we can add explanation to this, that the matter of the upper Daat is specifically in Chochmah,
unlike in Binah
(even though in Binah the matters of Chochmah are comprehended)
where it is the lower Daat,
for that in Chochmah is the upper Daat, where below there is not
(the feeling that everything before Him is considered as nothing),
is
(not from the aspect of its intellect,
for intellect is an existence,
the opposite of the feeling of being considered as nothing,
but rather)
from the aspect of its inwardness and essentiality
(which is analogous to the vision of Chochmah)
that is above intellect,
and since only the intellect of Chochmah is drawn into Binah,
therefore in Binah it is the lower Daat.
